checks.isa_semantics: GVSoC pulp_v2.hpp:1949-1956 p_clip_exec (register form): low = -rs2-1, high = rs2, then int.h lib_CLIP: a<low -> low, else a>high -> high, else a. pulp_v2.hpp:1958-1965 p_clipu_exec: high = rs2, then lib_CLIPU: a>high -> high, else a<=0 -> 0, else a. For b>=0, ~b<0<=b, so p.clipr equals both smin(smax(x,~b),b) and smax(smin(x,b),~b), and p.clipur equals smin(smax(x,0),b), smax(smin(x,b),0) and umin(smax(x,0),b), because smax(x,0)>=0 and for non-negative operands umin equals smin. For b<0 they differ exactly as the note says. The deleted betweenu is umin(umax(x,0),b) = umin(x,b); even with b>=0 it gives b for negative x where p.clipur gives 0, so it was wrong. It never fired: int-20 emits 0 p.clipur from plain C in both the worker's 13-kernel test (only the builtin) and my 28-kernel test.
checks.guard_soundness: SignBitIsZero only returns true when known-bits proves bit 31 is zero, so the pattern cannot fire for a bound that might be negative. Refusing constants in clipur_idiom is conservative. The repeated node:$bound is still checked as the same node: my k13 (lower bound ~c, upper bound b, both masked non-negative, c != b) is not turned into p.clipr.

checks.gap9_gcc_note: Found during review, not part of this task. GAP9 GCC miscompiles k16 'int t=x<0?0:x; return (unsigned)t>(unsigned)b?b:t;' into a single p.clipur a0,a0,a1 for a bound of unknown sign, which is wrong for negative b (e.g. x=-100000, b=INT_MIN gives INT_MIN, expected 0). So GAP9 GCC is not a reliable oracle for this shape. The worker build handles it correctly (no p.clipur).
